style_notes: Analog 35mm film photography, Kodak Portra 400 grain structure, heavily muted desaturated palette. Abstract and conceptual — never literal, never illustrative. No people, no faces, no obvious religious iconography. Evoke emotional and theological truth through texture, light, shadow, and negative space alone. Think Alabaster Books meets Kinfolk magazine: spare, intimate, unhurried. Objects minimal or absent. Light does the storytelling.
color_palette: Bleached linen, weathered stone, faded terracotta, dry grass, bone white, ash gray, deep shadow — all heavily desaturated with analog film warmth

cover.imageAlt: A long dusty road winding through pale dry hills at golden hour, empty, stretching toward an unseen horizon
cover.title: The Gospel of Luke
cover.concept: Luke is a journey. The road to Jerusalem structures the entire book — a long walk toward something unseen, with everything that matters happening along the way.
cover.prompt: 35mm analog film photograph, a long dusty unpaved road winding gently through pale dry hills at late golden hour, the road empty, no people, no vehicles, the horizon just barely visible in the far distance where the road disappears into haze, tall dry grass and scattered low brush at the edges of the road, long soft shadows stretching across the path, the light low, warm, and diffuse — almost exhausted — with heavy Kodak Portra 400 grain throughout, heavily muted and desaturated palette of weathered bone white, pale dry grass, soft ash gray, faded terracotta earth, deeply contemplative and unhurried, Alabaster Books aesthetic, Kinfolk editorial restraint, 16:9 landscape, the sky taking roughly the upper half of the frame with soft gradient from pale warm gold near the horizon to cool gray above, nothing to indicate era or location, timeless, quiet, the feeling of a journey about to begin or nearly ended
